forecast.revenue_drivers: FY2027E starts from 1H revenue of $177.8bn and Q3 guidance of $108.0bn excluding China Data Center compute [R1], with Q4 supported by Blackwell Ultra ramp [R18], Vera Rubin full production [R38] and $279bn supply commitments [R33]. FY2028E follows management's ~70% growth guidance [R6], backed by AI-cloud financing platforms targeting over $500bn [R39] and PORTS-Pike potentially representing $150-200bn per infrastructure generation [R36]. FY2029E fades to +35.3% as large-cloud capex growth slows toward ~40% or less in 2027 [R42] and China restrictions persist [R52][R53], partly offset by sovereign/enterprise demand and upgrade cycles [R36][R38].
forecast.margin_drivers: FY2027E gross margin ~73.7% blends 1H actual 75.0% [R15] (Q2 guided 74.9%/75.0% [R10]), Q3 guide 74.0% [R2] and Q4 trough 71-72% [R5][R12]; operating margin ~65.2% includes Q3 opex of ~$9.2bn [R3], and tax is 17.0% within the 16-18% FY2027 guide [R4]. FY2028E gross margin ~72.0% is held near the guided Q4 trough as memory procurement costs remain elevated [R33] and Vera Rubin transitions [R85], with operating margin ~64.0% on opex leverage; FY2029E gross margin ~71.5% and operating margin ~63.0% as competition/export mix offsets scale. Other income is 1.0% of revenue, excluding one-off equity gains [R44][R48].
forecast.vs_consensus: FY2027E revenue is in line with consensus $411.878bn (+90.7%); I use the 1H base and Q3 guide [R1]. FY2028E is ~1% above consensus $692.1bn because management guided ~70% growth [R6], not a broker extrapolation. FY2029E has no consensus in the input; I fade to +35.3% on capacity commitments [R33] and financing [R39] but decelerating hyperscale capex [R42] and China restrictions [R52][R53].
forecast.key_risk: The FY2028E ~70% growth and FY2029E +35.3% fade assume hyperscale/sovereign AI demand and NVIDIA's roadmap execute without a demand air-pocket or broader China restrictions. The most fragile leg is the capex/export assumption: Baird sees large-cloud capex growth slowing to ~40% or less in 2027 [R42], Goldman warns of data-center shell shortages by 2028 [R92], and H200 China restrictions could force a write-down [R95][R96]; early signals would be supply commitments stalling from $279bn [R33], Q4 gross margin missing the 71-72% trough [R5][R12], or a confirmed board/CEO disruption [R69][R71].

scenarios.name: bear
scenarios.drivers: For this case, the AI build-out has to peak during fiscal 2028. Baird's view that large-cloud capex growth slows to 40% or slightly less in 2027 [R42] and Goldman Sachs' warning that by 2028 there will not be enough data center shells [R92] would both have to come true. On top of that, the board's deliberations over removing CEO Jensen Huang [R69][R71] would push cloud providers toward AMD's custom designs [R82]. Harder pricing, which management flagged on the call [R97], memory-heavy supply commitments of $279 billion [R33] and a possible US$5 billion write-down on H200 inventory in Asia [R96] would then pull margins down. Probability: 30%, raised by the Baird downgrade to Neutral [R89], the US ban on Blackwell and Rubin exports to China [R52] and the leadership turmoil [R73], and held down by management's guidance of approximately 70% fiscal 2028 growth [R6] and Vera Rubin being in full production [R38].

scenarios.name: base
scenarios.drivers: In this case, NVIDIA delivers third-quarter revenue of $108.0 billion, plus or minus 2%, with no China Data Center compute assumed [R1]. It then meets management's guidance of approximately 70% growth for fiscal 2028 [R6] on the Blackwell Ultra ramp [R18] and Vera Rubin production [R38]. Probability: 50%, raised by the record Data Center revenue of $89.0 billion [R16] and the financing platforms aiming to mobilize over $500 billion [R39], and held down by the CEO investigation [R64] and China restrictions [R53].

scenarios.name: bull
scenarios.drivers: For this case, demand has to keep accelerating, as CEO Jensen Huang described with multiple frontier labs scaling in parallel [R38]. NVIDIA would also need to turn the PORTS-Pike campus into approximately $150 billion to $200 billion of revenue per infrastructure generation [R36], and the financing partnerships with Apollo, BlackRock, Blackstone, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs and KKR would need to fund the build-out beyond guidance [R39]. Scale would then lift the FCF margin back toward its three-year median. Probability: 20%, raised by the beat against consensus in the second quarter [R31] and President Donald Trump's backing of data center expansion [R58], and held down by Baird's capex slowdown view [R42] and the leadership uncertainty that William Blair says could benefit AMD [R80].

scenarios.note: Assumptions set by our analyst step from the research notes and the debate; the base case's revenue growth is our forecast's; values computed in code with the model's DCF (WACC 11.8%, terminal growth 2.5%, same net debt and share count). After year 3 the growth above terminal growth halves each year.

narrative.company_overview:
NVIDIA is a data center scale AI infrastructure company, selling accelerated computing platforms through two segments, Compute & Networking and Graphics. Its products span Data Center GPUs and networking, with Blackwell Ultra ramping and Vera Rubin in full production, plus gaming and professional visualisation graphics and automotive platforms such as DRIVE Hyperion.

Data Center was 89.7% (193.7bn) of FY2026 revenue of USD 215,938mn, with Gaming 7.4% (16.0bn); the United States was 69.3% (149.6bn) of revenue and Mainland China & Hong Kong 9.1% (19.7bn). Hyperscale was about 50% of Data Center revenue, with AI Clouds, enterprise and sovereign customers the rest. NVIDIA brings new advanced architectures on a one-year product cadence, and its latest-quarter operating margin was 65.2% against a 19.3% peer median.
narrative.financial_analysis:
1H FY2027 revenue rose 95.8% to 177,837mn and Q2 alone rose 105.9% to 96,221mn; gross margin reached 75.0% from 66.6% and operating profit rose 134.2% to 117,270mn. We forecast FY2027E revenue of 411,794mn (+90.7%), in line with consensus 411,878mn, FY2028E of 700,049mn (+70.0%, +1.1% vs consensus) on management's ~70% growth guidance, and FY2029E of 947,167mn (+35.3%) as we fade toward slower large-cloud capex. EPS is 10.27, 16.21 and 22.04. Gross margin eases from 73.7% to 71.5% as memory-heavy commitments of $279bn are consumed.

The five-year record shows operating margin rising from 37.3% in FY2022 to 60.4% in FY2026 and ROE of 101.5% in FY2026, but cash conversion of 0.86x in FY2026 and 0.63x in 1H FY2027. Net cash was 23,220mn at 26 Jul 2026 against 41,202mn at 25 Jan 2026, as cash and investments rose 6,916mn and debt rose 24,898mn.
narrative.valuation_overview:
The rating rests on the probability-weighted scenario value of USD 201.94: bear USD 81.25 at 30%, base USD 219.85 at 50% and bull USD 338.18 at 20%, with FCF margins of 36.0%, 42.0% and 45.0% assumed in the three cases. The model's mechanical DCF gives USD 222.40; our value is lower mainly because weighting the bear and bull cases costs USD 17.92, the bridge's largest step, and the bear scenario's assumptions cite Baird's capex view and Goldman's shell warning (press reports).

The reverse DCF shows the price needs 7.0% growth after FY2029 against our 10.2%, and the Monte Carlo puts the median at USD 219.52 with 65% of draws above the price. narrative.brief:
ANALYST BRIEF (the lead analyst's view, decided before writing: build the tagline, thesis, risks, valuation and rating text on it; every figure in it is from `facts`, `news` or `filings`):
- Central question: Does AI infrastructure demand hold up in fiscal 2029, after management's guided ~70% fiscal 2028 growth, or does the build-out peak?
- Our answer: Yes, at low conviction. Q2 Data Center revenue was a record $89.0 billion, up 117%. Management guides ~70% FY2028 growth, backed by $279 billion of supply commitments. We fade growth to +35.3% in FY2029, not a collapse.
- What the price implies: The reverse DCF shows today's price implies revenue growth of 7.0% a year from FY2029 to FY2036, against 10.2% in our base case. The stock trades at 10.9x forward P/E against a peer median of 20.4x. Over 90 days, FY2028E EPS rose +24.1% while the P/E fell from 17.5x to 10.9x. That is a de-rating, not lower estimates.
- Pillar 1: Demand is visible through fiscal 2028, not just the guided quarter. Evidence: Data Center revenue for the second quarter was a record $89.0 billion, up 117%; fiscal 2028 revenue growth of approximately 70%; supply and capacity commitments increased from $119 billion to $279 billion. Breaks if: Q3 revenue lands below the $108.0 billion ±2% guide, or management withdraws ~70% FY2028 growth.
- Pillar 2: The price already discounts a slower path than ours. Evidence: Reverse DCF implies 7.0% growth FY2029–FY2036 vs our base 10.2%; P/E forward 10.9x vs peer median 20.4x; P/E on FY2028E EPS moved from 17.5x to 10.9x. Breaks if: Consensus FY2028E EPS of 15.93 is cut, turning the de-rating into an earnings downgrade.
- Pillar 3: Downside is large enough to keep the Buy borderline. Evidence: Bear USD 81.25 (30%); guarantees, maximum exposure USD 108.5bn; Baird sees large-cloud capex growth slowing to 40% or slightly less in 2027. Breaks if: The bear probability rises from 30% to 32%, which moves the rating to Hold.
- Beyond our forecast years: After FY2029, excess growth halves every year. In the bear case, the build-out peaks in fiscal 2028, revenue falls 10.0% and the FCF margin is 36.0%, as Goldman warns of too few data-center shells by 2028. In the bull case, PORTS-Pike yields $150 billion to $200 billion per generation and the FCF margin is 45.0%.
- Revenue and profit quality: 1H FY2027 gains on investments of USD 23.7bn, about 20% of net profit, are non-cash fair-value changes. Use operating profit growth of +134.2%, not net profit's +161.1%. Cash conversion fell to 0.63x from 0.95x. The maximum exposure under guarantees is USD 108.5bn, including the $105 billion PORTS-Pike cap with OpenAI as tenant, so some revenue is self-supported.
- Governance: Reported after the 11 Nov price: the WSJ said the board was preparing to oust CEO Jensen Huang, who admitted an affair with Alice Huang of Megaspeed. The board said it is investigating whether he was a foreign-intelligence target, sees no compromised secrets and has confidence in him. Outcome unconfirmed.
- Where we differ from the brokers: The brokers' median target is USD 317.00. Our FY2028E EPS is only +1.8% above consensus, so the gap lies after the guided years. We give 30% weight to a bear case in which FY2029 revenue falls 10.0%, on Baird's capex view and Goldman's shell warning. That is the value bridge's largest step (-17.92).
- What to watch: Results on 17 Nov: guidance is $108.0 billion ±2% against consensus of USD 109,007mn, with a gross margin of 74.0%. Options price about ±9.3%. The deciding item is reaffirmation of ~70% FY2028 growth and the Q4 71% to 72% margin trough. Also watch the board's decision on Huang. A cut to FY2028 growth would mean Hold.
- Tagline (by the lead analyst; use it as the report's tagline as written): The market prices an AI capex peak; the evidence says demand outlasts fiscal 2028 guidance, narrowly.
- Thesis paragraph (by the lead analyst; use it as the thesis, changing only what a rule or `feedback` requires; a deep report adds one sentence on the debate's verdict and swing factor): NVIDIA turns on whether AI infrastructure demand survives past fiscal 2028, the last year management has guided. We think growth slows rather than stalls. The price implies 7.0% annual growth after the consensus years, below the 10.2% in our base case: the market is pricing a capex peak. Quality needs watching. Accounting gains on equity stakes lift net profit, cash conversion has weakened, and NVIDIA now guarantees parts of its customers' build-out. Our probability-weighted value of USD 201.94 supports a Buy, but a borderline one held with low confidence: shifting two points of probability to the bear case makes it a Hold. We sit well below the brokers because we give 30% weight to a fiscal 2029 revenue decline. Reports of a possible CEO ouster emerged after our price date and are not yet reflected.

company.description: NVIDIA Corporation operates as a data center scale AI infrastructure company in the United States, Taiwan, China, Hong Kong, Europe, and internationally. It operates through Compute & Networking, and Graphics segments. The Compute & Networking segment provides data center accelerated computing and networking platforms and artificial intelligence solutions and software, and automotive platforms and autonomous and electric vehicle solutions, including software. The Graphics segment offers GeForce GPUs for gaming and PCs; Quadro/NVIDIA RTX GPUs for enterprise workstation graphics. The company's products are used in gaming, professional visualization, data center, and automotive markets. It sells its products to original equipment manufacturers, original device manufacturers, system integrators and distributors, independent software vendors, cloud service providers, add-in board manufacturers, distributors, automotive manufacturers and tier-1 automotive suppliers, and other ecosystem participants. It has a collaboration with Cisco to develop Ultra-Dense Small Form Factor Pluggable (USFP), a high-density optical module pluggable transceiver. It has a collaboration with ChipAgents to develop Build-A-Chip-Bench, a benchmark for AI agents carrying chip design tasks and The Company has a strategic alliance with MediaTek to build the next generations of AI computing platforms. NVIDIA Corporation was incorporated in 1993 and is headquartered in Santa Clara, California.
